issues.t: Internal water pump failure mixing coolant and oil
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping with no visible puddle, coolant seeping from behind the front engine cover, milky oil, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: The water pump sits inside the engine and is driven by the timing chain. When its seal fails, coolant can leak into the oil instead of onto the ground.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats or the oil looks milky. Have a slow coolant loss checked early, because coolant in the oil can ruin the engine bearings.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit leaks and overheating
issues.sym: A burnt gear-oil smell after driving, thick dark fluid dripping behind the engine, or whining and grinding from the front.
issues.why: The power transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels sits close to the exhaust and holds little oil. Its seals can leak and the fluid can cook and break down.
issues.next: Have the unit and its seals inspected and the fluid changed if it is dark or low. A unit that runs dry can fail.

issues.t: Transmission speed sensor faults
issues.sym: Harsh engagement, no upshift, the transmission stuck in one gear, and a check engine light with sensor codes.
issues.why: The input or output speed sensors in the 6-speed automatic can give faulty readings, so the transmission computer cannot shift properly. Ford issued a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the sensors tested. Fixing the sensor problem early can prevent more costly transmission work.

issues.t: Transmission range sensor problems
issues.sym: Slipping into neutral, starting off in a high gear, a wrong gear shown on the dash, the backup camera turning on in Drive, or cruise control cutting out.
issues.why: The sensor that tells the computer which gear the shifter is in can send wrong signals. Ford issued a service bulletin for the fault.
issues.next: Have it checked promptly. A car that drops into neutral or does not know its gear is unsafe, so limit driving until it is repaired.

issues.t: Brake booster diaphragm tear (extended warranty)
issues.sym: A hissing sound from under the dash when pressing the brake pedal and a pedal that becomes harder to push, so stopping takes more effort.
issues.why: A small tear can form in the brake booster diaphragm and grow over time, reducing the power assist to the brakes. Ford extended the warranty on the booster for certain vehicles.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked right away if the pedal gets hard or you hear hissing. Ask a Ford dealer whether the extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Door ajar light stays on and drains the battery
issues.sym: The door ajar warning stays lit with all doors shut, interior lights stay on, the doors may relock or unlock on their own, and the battery goes dead overnight.
issues.why: A switch built into a door latch can fail and keep telling the car that a door is open. Ford issued a service bulletin for it.
issues.next: Have the faulty door latch identified and replaced. Until then, watch for a dead battery and check that every door actually latches.

issues.t: MyFord Touch screen freezes or goes black
issues.sym: The center touchscreen freezes, reboots, responds slowly, or goes black, along with phone, audio or navigation features that stop working.
issues.why: The MyFord Touch and SYNC software and its control module had many bugs. Ford released software updates and some cars needed the module replaced.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to install the latest software. If the screen keeps failing after the update, the control module may need replacing.

issues.t: Front halfshaft can disconnect (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power to the wheels, a clunk from the front, or the vehicle rolling while in Park.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the halfshaft may not have been fully seated at the factory, so the shaft can slide out. Ford recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and always use the parking brake when parked until it is repaired.

issues.t: Front brake hoses can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stopping distances, a brake warning light, or fluid on the inside of a front wheel.
issues.why: The front brake hoses can wear through and burst. Ford's fix is a hose with stronger braiding.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If the pedal feels soft, stop driving and have the vehicle towed.

issues.t: Rear brake hose can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, a brake warning light, or brake fluid leaking near a rear wheel.
issues.why: A rear brake hose that flexes with the suspension can rupture and leak brake fluid. This is a separate recall from the front hoses.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall too. If the pedal feels soft or fluid is leaking, stop driving and have the vehicle towed.

issues.t: Coolant leaking into the cylinders
issues.sym: White exhaust smoke or a misfire at cold start, a check engine light, a coolant level that keeps dropping with no outside leak, or overheating.
issues.why: Owners and class action lawsuits report that coolant can seep into the combustion chambers on this engine, which can lead to cracked heads or engine failure.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level closely. If it keeps dropping with no visible leak, stop driving and have a cooling system pressure test and cylinder leak-down test done.

issues.t: AWD intermediate shaft seal leak
issues.sym: Dark fluid dripping near the right front of the transmission, sometimes with a burning smell if it lands on the exhaust.
issues.why: A seal on the right-side intermediate shaft at the power transfer unit can leak. Ford issued a service bulletin, and the repair requires removing the unit.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the fluid level checked. Repair it before the unit runs low on oil.

issues.t: Torque converter studs can break (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling from the transmission area, loss of drive power while moving, or the vehicle not holding in Park.
issues.why: Studs welded to the torque converter may not have been welded properly and can snap. Ford issued recalls.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and always set the parking brake until it is fixed.

issues.t: Shifter cable bushing can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the transmission is not in the gear shown, or the car rolls after being put in Park.
issues.why: The bushing that links the shift cable to the transmission can break down or pop off.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the bushing before relying on Park.

issues.t: Power steering motor bolts can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that suddenly turns heavy with a power steering warning, mostly in road-salt regions.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the bolts that hold the electric steering motor to the steering gear, letting the motor come loose.
issues.next: You can still steer with more effort. Have a dealer check the VIN and replace or seal the bolts.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak from start-stop accumulator (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the front of the car, a burning smell, or slipping shifts.
issues.why: Bolts on the end cap of the transmission accumulator used for auto start-stop may be loose or missing, letting fluid leak onto hot parts.
issues.next: If you see a fluid leak or smell burning, stop driving and have it towed. Check the VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or stuck on (recalls)
issues.sym: No picture in Reverse, a distorted picture, or the camera view staying on after you shift out of Reverse.
issues.why: A software fault, and on some 2020 cars a poor electrical connection at the camera, interrupts the image.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look back when reversing. A dealer can check the VIN and update software or replace the camera.

issues.t: Driver seat belt anchor may be badly crimped (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing noticeable in normal use.
issues.why: The anchor for the driver seat belt pretensioner may not have been crimped properly, so the belt could pull free in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a Ford dealer and have the pretensioner replaced if the recall is open.

issues.t: AWD rear drive unit low on oil can seize (recall)
issues.sym: Whine or grinding from the rear, then the rear wheels may lock or the car may lose drive.
issues.why: Some all-wheel-drive rear drive units were filled with too little lubricant at the factory.
issues.next: If you hear rear-end grinding, stop driving. Have a dealer check the VIN and the rear drive unit.

issues.t: Intake valves can break in the 2.7L engine (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden misfire, loud engine noise and loss of power, often with no earlier warning.
issues.why: A batch of intake valves in the 2.7L turbo V6 can crack and break, destroying the engine.
issues.next: If the engine suddenly runs rough or loses power, pull over and shut it off. Have a dealer check the VIN and test the engine.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank, frozen or delayed (recalls)
issues.sym: The big touchscreen shows no picture, a frozen picture or a late picture when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: Software faults, and an accessory module that can overheat and shut down, interrupt the rear camera display.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look back when reversing. Have a dealer check the VIN and apply the latest software.

issues.t: Rear seat child tether anchor may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing noticeable until a child seat is tethered in the left rear seat.
issues.why: The welds on the tether anchor wire of the second-row left seat back may be too weak to hold a child seat in a crash.
issues.next: Use another seating position for a tethered child seat until a dealer has checked the VIN and repaired the seat.

issues.t: Right headlight may be misaimed or too bright (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash their lights at you, or the right beam points noticeably high.
issues.why: The front right headlight on some cars does not meet the federal brightness and aim standard.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have a dealer check the VIN and correct or replace the headlight.
